gpu_to_cpu_vram_decrease.cycle_stability_evidence: every retirement-to-CPU step in cycle_stability.json's 50-cycle run shows VRAM dropping back to the CPU-side baseline (429 MiB) from the GPU-side value (433-435 MiB) -- a clean, real, repeated drop.

cpu_side_rss_decrease: Not independently isolated in this phase's experiments (all cycle/multi-layer trials measure RSS across the WHOLE alternating CPU<->GPU cycle, not isolated to a single CPU-retirement step) -- cycle_stability.json's RSS figures show no net growth trend across 50 full round trips, which is consistent with (but does not in isolation prove) real host-RAM reclamation on each GPU->CPU retirement specifically.
allocator_granularity_honesty: 1/2/4/8-layer VRAM reclamation at ctx=8192/135M (6, 9, 15, 28 MiB respectively) is slightly super-linear per-layer at small counts (6 MiB for 1 layer vs a theoretical ~1.3 MiB of raw K+V bytes at this ctx) -- consistent with a fixed per-allocation Vulkan allocator/driver overhead on top of the raw tensor bytes, the same allocator-overhead pattern already disclosed in Phase 12C/12D's own VRAM accounting. At the ctx=200000/360M pressure-regime scale, reclaimed VRAM (132 MiB) is much closer to the raw layer byte size (~130 MiB, matching Phase 12D's own measurement for this exact layer/config), since fixed overhead is proportionally smaller at that scale.
